title: Short AAPL — WWDC 2026 Sell-the-News; Distribution Above $300 Confirmed
entry: Short $298–305 (AAPL at $301.54 June 8 close). Initiate on any morning bounce toward $302–305 that stalls on declining volume — the WWDC gap-and-fail pattern creates one more false-recovery entry point before distribution resumes. Do NOT short below $298 — below $298 the position overlaps the morning briefing's 'better entry' stabilization zone of $295–300 where the distribution thesis may pause before resuming.
stop_loss: $315 daily close (~+4.5% above entry midpoint $301.50) — implies a follow-on Apple Intelligence product announcement (concrete iPhone 17 AI-hardware launch date, AI App Store revenue model revealed) overrides the sell-the-news dynamic; also triggered if SPX closes above 7,460 and VIX closes below 17 on CPI relief
targets: $290 — WWDC euphoria fully fades over 3–5 sessions; no new AAPL-specific catalyst; macro STEP ASIDE regime unchanged; –3.8% from entry midpoint $301.50
$280 — hot CPI Wednesday June 10 compresses Nasdaq multiples; AAPL's ~30x forward P/E (pricing an AI revenue stream that doesn't yet exist) corrects toward 27x alongside the tape; –7.1%

$268 — Warsh June 17 FOMC signals or delivers first rate hike; broad distribution in mega-cap tech resumes; AAPL, which lacks the earnings-catalyst path that partially protects NVDA or MSFT in a rate-hike scenario, de-rates faster than peers; –11.1%
catalyst: Apple's WWDC 2026 keynote on June 8 unveiled 'Apple Intelligence' — an AI-powered next-generation Siri and a suite of on-device/cloud hybrid AI capabilities developed in partnership with Google (Gemini integration). The initial intraday reaction was a spike to $317 (+5.2% from Friday); the close was $301.54 (−1.89%). The sell-the-news pattern is textbook: a multi-week run-up into the event (AAPL was ~$285 in late May), maximum retail enthusiasm at the keynote, and institutional distribution through the session as the event de-risks the position. The morning briefing explicitly places AAPL on the 'Don't Buy Right Now' list and identifies $295–300 as the stabilization entry for bulls — implying the $301–305 range is the clean short entry before that stabilization occurs.
thesis:
AAPL's $301.54 close on June 8 is a distribution event, not a buying opportunity. The pattern is structurally identical to prior WWDC sell-the-news cycles: a company reveals its next platform narrative, institutional holders who positioned for the event use the spike to exit at maximum crowd participation, and retail enthusiasm sustains the open while the close reveals where conviction actually lies. The fact that AAPL gave back the entire WWDC spike — from $317 intraday to $301.54 close, a 5.2% reversal — in a session where the S&P 500 was positive confirms that the 'Apple Intelligence' reveal met institutional selling rather than accumulation.

The valuation structure makes the distribution thesis durable rather than one-day. AAPL trades at approximately $3.0T market cap on ~$400B annual revenue (≈7.5x revenue) and approximately 30x forward earnings. The 30x forward P/E prices in an AI-driven iPhone supercycle — but 'Apple Intelligence' as revealed at WWDC 2026 is a software upgrade that requires no new hardware purchase until iPhone 17 (September 2026 at earliest). The supercycle narrative is therefore a 3–6 month forward event at best. At the current multiple, AAPL is pricing the supercycle now, which means the near-term re-rating direction is lower, not higher, as the market reassesses the revenue timeline.

The macro overlay reinforces the short from two angles. First, the CPI binary on Wednesday June 10 creates a specific risk for high-multiple consumer tech: a hot print (+4.2%+ YoY) compresses valuation multiples as rate-hike probability rises. AAPL at ~30x PE is one of the most multiple-sensitive large-caps in the tape — more so than NVDA (which has explicit near-term earnings growth to partially defend its multiple) or MSFT (which has Azure AI revenue already flowing). Second, the Warsh June 17 FOMC rate hike risk is specifically adverse for companies with consumer-facing cyclical exposure (iPhone demand is rate-sensitive: consumers finance purchases) and for consumer-tech P/E multiples broadly.

The counter-party is the AAPL bull who believes the Apple Intelligence ecosystem — on-device AI running locally, Gemini cloud integration, new Siri capabilities — will drive the most significant iPhone upgrade cycle since Face ID in 2017. That thesis is directionally correct on a 12-month horizon. This short exploits specifically the 1–2 week post-WWDC distribution mechanics, not a fundamental short on AAPL's long-term AI positioning.
bull_case: Apple announces a concrete iPhone 17 pre-order opening date or an Apple Intelligence hardware accessory within the WWDC week — a 'supercycle starts now' catalyst that restores the narrative immediately. CPI prints cool (≤3.8% core); VIX falls below 17; SPX closes above 7,460. AAPL short-covers to $310–315; stop triggered at $315.
bear_case: Hot CPI Wednesday (+4.3%+ YoY) compresses consumer-tech multiples; AAPL trades to $285–290 within two sessions of the print. AAPL management provides no iPhone 17 timeline or AI hardware catalyst at WWDC follow-on events. Warsh June 17 FOMC signals rate hike; AAPL multiple compresses from ~30x to 27x; stock moves toward $268 (Target 3).
invalidation: $315 daily close, OR AAPL announces a concrete iPhone 17 AI-hardware launch date at or before June 17 (supercycle narrative becomes near-term), OR CPI Wednesday prints ≤3.5% core (macro relief overrides the sell-news momentum)
